A.trend: Full traced 24-month series with the window stated. Both Nov 2024 peaks are named and peak-to-latest falls (64.7%, 48.1%) recompute exactly. Critical share is decomposed and also traced.
A.comparison: Same call and window throughout. Ratios and deltas recompute (1.035, +765, 0.65), the baseline is defined, the overlap caveat is carried, and the reading says this is attention, not business performance.
A.chart: Volume chart and critical-share chart are both fully traced, overlaid per term, with window, unit and source. The censored month is correctly excluded.
A.drilldown: One traced layer (period and tone class). Only 1 of 7 follow-ups executed, and no item-level identifiers.
A.export: Monthly and summary CSVs are fully traced, with source, window, unit and coverage. Period ids are included, the provenance JSON is present, and both files are referenced.
A.repro: 82 of 88 numbers traced, the call is listed with args, and derived figures are shown. A few figures (coverage 107.1%, the Eternal note) are not in the reference.
A.accuracy: Peaks, lead counts (13/24, 6 of last 8), the critical percentages and the 144-day gap all check. Undefined fields are flagged and the tone_ratio inference is labelled. No anomaly beyond that is caught.
A.limits: Window, censoring, gap to today, match mode, overlap and the Eternal alias are each stated next to the numbers they bound.
A.verdict: Direct answer, decision, confidence with reason, and what would change it. It names the contrary recent Swiggy lead and stays under 150 words.
A.facets: Volume, share, trend, tone, overlap and the Eternal rename are all addressed. The overlap and the alias are not measurable from the data.

B.accuracy: Two misreadings: it calls combined_articles a de-duplicated union (it is the plain sum), and it treats 'Zomato' as a common word.
B.limits: Specific about what is unmeasured, and the Eternal alias is a good catch.
B.facets: Facets come mostly from memory or are left blank.

C.trend: Uses only the first and last points although all were available. The peak is not named. The endpoint change is wrongly called provisional because of an 'incomplete' month.
C.comparison: Traced 1.035 ratio and 765 delta with the baseline defined and the attention caveat carried.
C.chart: Volume chart only. Tone was available but is not charted.
C.drilldown: One aggregate layer, and follow-ups mostly fail.
C.export: Traced CSVs with provenance, but coverage=partial is mislabelled and the window end is given as inclusive of 2026-06.
C.repro: 32 of 34 traced, with the call and args listed.
C.accuracy: Misreads censoring: it claims May 2026 is incomplete, but May is partial_period:false and June was already censored.
C.limits: The window and gap to today are stated, but the censoring limit is misapplied.
C.verdict: Supported answer, but its confidence rests on a misread incomplete month. It does not cover tone.
C.facets: Tone is only lightly read. Eternal is not addressed.

D.accuracy: No contradictions because it makes no claims.

A: Coverage figure of 107.1% is not visible in the reference record.
B: Calls combined_articles a de-duplicated union; it equals the sum of the two term totals.
Calls 'Zomato' a common first word in other contexts.
C: Claims the latest displayed month (2026-05) is incomplete; the reference marks it partial_period:false, and the censored month is 2026-06.

raw.verdict: A read the full traced series correctly. It named the peaks, computed exact declines and lead changes, decomposed tone, and flagged the Eternal rename and the overlap. C used the same data but compared only endpoints and misread the censoring, treating May 2026 as incomplete. B and D measured nothing; B also misdescribed combined_articles.
